mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, investors anticipate tighter credit conditions, which reduces the present value of future earnings and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in similar rising-rate regimes are not statistically lower than in neutral periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months signals disinflation, prompting central banks to hold rates steady and reducing risk aversion, which tends to drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during previous inflationary periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs in a month coincides with rising consumer confidence and corporate hiring intentions, which amplifies equity valuation multiples and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In analogous strong-labor-market regimes, 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than in weak-labor-market periods (IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 5% in a month indicates weakening manufacturing demand, which reduces earnings expectations and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% in a single month
failure_condition: During comparable demand shocks, 5-day forward returns are not persistently negative (IC < 0.10 over 30 days).

mechanism_narrative: When residential mortgage applications (HOUST) fall by more than 10% in a month, it signals deteriorating housing demand and increased loan supply risk, which elevates equity market volatility and tends to produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by >10% in a month
failure_condition: In similar supply shocks, 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than in normal periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both retail sales (RSAFS) and industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 3% in the same month indicate a dual-demand shock, which amplifies recessionary expectations and tends to drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < RSAFS_prev_month AND INDPRO < INDPRO_prev_month by ≥3%
failure_condition: In analogous dual-demand episodes, 60-day forward returns are not significantly more negative than in single-demand shocks (IC > 0.10 over 60 days).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4.5% for three consecutive months indicates a strengthening labor market that spurs central bank tightening, which compresses discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: During comparable labor-market-weakening phases, 20-day forward returns are not persistently negative (IC > 0.10 over 60 days).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) exceed 300,000 by double digits, it signals robust labor absorption and optimism about economic growth, which elevates equity risk premia and tends to drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month
failure_condition: In analogous strong-labor-absorption regimes, 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than in moderate-growth regimes (IC > 0.05).
